items.summary: Chan has argued that technology can help extend the audience for existing journalism, but that reporting still depends on people’s ability to build trust, draw out personal accounts and make editorial decisions. The Associated Press similarly says AI may assist newsroom work but does not replace journalists’ responsibility for gathering and assessing facts. Its standards require staff to verify AI-generated material and remain accountable for published work; ProPublica also says AI-assisted [...] One early application of AI is helping SPH Media make its reporting available to readers who do not speak the original language. Lianhe Zaobao has launched an English-language website using AI-assisted translation alongside human proofreading and editing. The publication says the initiative is designed to bring its reporting and analysis to younger readers and people from other language communities, while preserving its Chinese-language edition. Malay and Tamil-language offerings are expected [...] The publisher is partnering with Google and using AI-assisted translation to reach new audiences, while warning that AI could make news organisations less visible to readers.

items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary: “SMASH UP” genuinely unsettled Symphony Hall. Iron-sounding trumpets clashed with the mellow strings. The culmination of the movement was an ear-shattering climax — the brass utterly razing any semblance of prior peace. But the following movements, inseparable from their AI participation, were less captivating. Delays between the musicians’ playing and the system’s processing limited their musical conversation — they lacked any shared sound. The music of the orchestra was divided from the odd, [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra.

items.title: SPS to tighten student tech policies this week for students in grades 3 to 5
items.summary:
SEATTLE — Seattle Public Schools (SPS) is tightening its technology rules for some students this week, adding new limits aimed at reducing distractions and curbing reliance on generative AI tools.

Superintendent Ben Shuldiner said that when he arrived in Seattle, it was clear the district had “steered too heavily into an overreliance of technology.” [...] RELATED | Seattle schools to cap elementary students' screen time, block unapproved AI tools

Parents have been asking the district to review how technology is used in classrooms, saying students are getting distracted or relying too heavily on generative AI tools. [...] Under the changes, students in grades three through five will have a one-hour daily cap on screen time. The limit includes activities such as watching a 10-minute educational video.

The district will also no longer allow iPads and laptops to be used as incentives or rewards. In addition, Seattle Public Schools is blocking access to Minecraft, YouTube and Gemini, programs Shuldiner said have been "abused."

However, regulators in China and the U.S. must approve the tie-up, a process management expects could stretch into early 2028. Analysts also warned that Lumentum competes with several of [...] ## What's next for Marvell Technology

Investors will get their next operational update when Marvell reports fiscal third-quarter results on Dec. 1, 2026. Management narrowed its preliminary quarterly revenue guidance to approximately $3.2 billion, but near-term financial results are taking a back seat to deal execution risks. items.summary:
this is f*cking insane. andrej karpathy: "the biggest regret of every engineer in my field right now is every AI conversation they never saved, and in 10 years the ones who started saving in 2024 will be running circles around the rest of us"

andrej karpathy, co-founder of openai, pulled 16M views on one idea: stop using AI to write code, use it to build a second brain that remembers every article, pdf, transcript and conversation you ever fed it

you point claude code at a folder, drop anything into it, and claude reads it, cross-links it with everything already there, and writes it into a living wiki. your knowledge finally compounds instead of leaking out of your head every friday

the stack:

→ brew install obsidian, mkdir ~/vault, cd ~/vault
→ run claude in that folder and type "init a knowledge vault with CLAUDE.md as the rules, /raw for sources, /wiki for your pages"
→ drop any file into /raw (youtube transcript, meeting notes, 400-page pdf, screenshot of a tweet) and type "ingest"
→ claude writes a wiki page, links it to 5 existing ones automatically, updates CLAUDE.md with any new pattern it noticed about how you think
→ never open a blank claude chat again. every question goes through the vault, every answer cites your own sources with dates and links

5 minutes to set up. compounding knowledge from that evening forward

the ugly part most will scroll past: in 10 years the engineers who started this in 2024 will remember every book, every podcast, every meeting with receipts. you will remember none of them. karpathy already picked which side he is on and you are still not on his

Its standards require staff to verify AI-generated material and remain accountable for published work; ProPublica also says AI-assisted [...] One early application of AI is helping SPH Media make its reporting available to readers who do not speak the original language. The publication says the initiative is designed to bring its reporting and analysis to younger readers and people from other language communities, while preserving its Chinese-language edition. items.title: The BSO Meets AI, and Explores the Vitality of Classical Music Today | The Harvard Crimson
items.summary: “SMASH UP” genuinely unsettled Symphony Hall. Iron-sounding trumpets clashed with the mellow strings. The culmination of the movement was an ear-shattering climax — the brass utterly razing any semblance of prior peace. But the following movements, inseparable from their AI participation, were less captivating. Delays between the musicians’ playing and the system’s processing limited their musical conversation — they lacked any shared sound. The music of the orchestra was divided from the odd, [...] From Oct. 22 to 24, the Boston Symphony Orchestra and conductor Kent Nagano performed “already and not yet: A world premiere by Tod Machover.” The headliner was a modern classical work: an onstage musical dialogue between the BSO and a live AI system. Beyond the philosophical implications of the concept, the performance struck at a key nerve of classical music culture — a delicate balancing of tradition and relevance. [...] At the center of Machover’s composition philosophy is his belief that classical music finds a natural extension and innovation in technology. He revealed in an interview with GBH music that the music he hears in his head is often beyond the scope of traditional instruments. Thus, alongside the MIT Media Lab, Machover has developed an audio AI that takes in the playing of the orchestra as input and produces live synthetic sounds that — as Machover puts it — “enhances” the orchestra.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI kicks off charm offensive to change voters' view of data centers | Reuters
items.summary:
SAN FRANCISCO, Nov 5 (Reuters) - Stunning ​victories by Democrats in US midterm elections this week have been interpreted by many as Americans repudiating tech ‌industry plans to build data centers across the country. OpenAI has now embarked on new strategies to change their minds.

The AI lab on Thursday laid out policies — in the works since August — intended to help the company build more trust with local communities and convince them that data centers will ​benefit them. [...] OpenAI officials, along with many of their peers in tech, ​have spent the last ⁠two years trying to build ties with the administration of US President Donald Trump in hopes of shaping federal policy around AI.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman donated $1 million to Trump's inaugural committee and later attended Trump's second inauguration. Last year, Brockman donated $25 million in his personal capacity to ⁠a Trump ​super PAC. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

OpenAI said it will no longer use non-disclosure agreements with public officials when negotiating or discussing future sites, although ​proprietary information would still be under wraps. It will also give residents access to construction plans ⁠and their potential effect on traffic, noise and lighting.

items.title: OpenAI will keep investing in AI data centers despite election results, CFO tells CNBC
items.summary:
OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar on Friday said the company will continue to invest in artificial intelligence infrastructure, even after voters strongly rebuked data centers during Tuesday's midterm elections. [...] OpenAI depends on data centers to train its AI models and serve customers, and Friar said she doesn't think the midterms dramatically changed anything for the company.

"If the midterm means more focus on data centers and communities, we're going to keep doing the work to get into those communities and to build trust with them," Friar said. [...] "When I think about the midterms, I need to keep thinking about how do we keep investing to meet that customer demand," Friar told CNBC's Sara Eisen in an interview at the Citi TMT Leadership Summit at California's Pebble Beach. "It starts early with having built relationships with all of the hyperscalers, and it will continue to mean that we raise capital."
